title: AI policy
excerpt: Where AI tooling is used on this site, where it is not, and how an AI-assisted page is checked before it ships.
meta_title: AI policy — where AI is used on Onim, and where it is not
meta_description: How Onim uses AI tooling for drafting and code review, what is never left to a model, and how AI-assisted pages are checked before publishing.
content:
Some of the writing and code on Onim is drafted with the help of AI tools, and some is not. This page says which is which, how the two are kept apart, and what happens when an AI-assisted draft turns out to be wrong. It exists because "AI-generated" and "written by a person" are not useful answers on their own.

The short version

  • No answer on this site is produced by an AI model at the moment you use it. Every calculator runs a formula that is written down and checked. Nothing you type is sent to a language model.
  • The explanations are human-reviewed. Articles, worked examples and the "what the result means" sections are drafted by the team and, where AI tooling was used for a first draft or a structural pass, the final text is read and corrected by a person who is named as responsible for the page.
  • Formulas are never left to a model. An equation, a unit conversion or a tax band is taken from a source, written by hand, and tested against a worked example with a known answer.
  • Your inputs and files are never used to train anything. Calculator values stay in your browser. Files opened in a tool never leave your device. No message you send is fed to a model.

Where AI tooling is used

Drafting and editing

A first draft of an explanatory section may be produced with an AI writing tool from an outline supplied by the team — the formula, the variables, the assumptions and the reference the article has to agree with. The draft is then edited by a person, checked against the source, and rewritten where it is vague, padded or wrong. A page that has not been through that pass is not published.

Code review and testing

AI assistants are used as a second pair of eyes on code: to look for a missing edge case, an unhandled unit, a rounding error or a layout that breaks at a narrow width. They do not decide what a calculator does. Every formula, every unit table and every validation rule is human-specified, and the tests that decide whether a page ships are written by hand and run against known answers.

Images

The photographs on the About page were generated for this site rather than licensed from a stock library. They are illustrative portraits of the team, not photographs taken with a camera, and the About page says so. Diagram figures on calculator pages are drawn as SVG from the formula they illustrate, not generated from a prompt.

Translations and accessibility fixes

Short interface strings and alt-text may be drafted with assistance and checked by a person. Alt-text for a diagram is written from the diagram's actual content, because a caption that describes the wrong chart is worse than no caption.

Where AI tooling is not used

  • Calculation. The solver that computes a result is deterministic code. The same inputs give the same answer on every visit, and the formula is printed on the page so you can check it by hand.
  • Medical, financial and legal framing. The passages that tell you what a result does and does not mean are written or signed off by the person responsible for that subject area, not generated.
  • Decisions about you. There is no automated decision-making about visitors, no scoring, no profiling and no personalisation driven by a model.
  • Moderation of your messages. Contact messages and reviews are read by a person. Spam rules are plain, published rules (no links in reviews, a rate limit per address), not a model's judgement.

How an AI-assisted page is checked before it ships

  1. The formula is fixed first. It comes from a textbook, a standard, a datasheet or a regulator's published rule, and the source is named on the page.
  2. The worked example is computed independently. By hand, in a spreadsheet or from the source's own example — never by the code being tested.
  3. Every field is exercised. Ordinary values, boundary values, a value that is out of range and a letter where a number belongs. A wrong entry gets a message under the field; it does not quietly produce a zero.
  4. The prose is read against the formula. If the article says "halve the diameter and the area falls by four", someone checks that the equation actually does that.
  5. The page is read on a phone. Long formulas and wide tables have a habit of being unreadable at 390 pixels wide, which is a correctness problem on a tool site.
  6. A person signs off. The page carries the date it was last updated, and a correction goes into the page rather than into a footnote.

What happens when AI-assisted work is wrong

It gets fixed the same way any other error does: the page is corrected, the worked example is re-run, and if the mistake came from a repeated pattern — a unit table copied wrongly, a rounding rule applied in the wrong place — every page that shares the pattern is checked. A wrong result is a bug on this site, not a disclaimer. If you find one, the contact form takes the calculator name, the values you entered and the answer you expected.

Copyright and sources

Text on this site is written for it. Formulas, unit definitions and regulatory thresholds are facts and are not owned by anyone; where a page leans on a specific source, the source is named. We do not reproduce long passages from other websites, and we do not use AI tooling to rewrite someone else's article into a "new" one. If you believe a page reproduces your work, tell us and it will be checked and removed if the complaint is right.

What we will not do with AI

  • We will not put a generated answer in place of a calculation and present it as computed.
  • We will not invent a quotation, a study, a reviewer or a user testimonial.
  • We will not generate medical, legal or financial advice and dress it as a result of a formula.
  • We will not use a model to make a decision about whether your message is spam and then refuse to show you why.
  • We will not train anything on the values you enter or the files you open, because we do not receive them.

Keeping this page honest

If a page on this site looks machine-written in the bad sense — confident, vague, restating the heading, unable to say where a number comes from — that page is unfinished. Send the address through the contact form and it will be rewritten. The About page describes who writes what, and the privacy policy describes what the site does with data.
